\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{به} \fa{دلیل} (be dalil-e)}{به دلیل (be dalil-e)}]{\fa{به} \fa{دلیل} (be dalil-e) — because of, due to}

\label{lesson:FA-C371-be-dalil-e}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to lead to, then the Persian for to conclude.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{به} \fa{دلیل}}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{دلیل}} (\emph{be dalil-e}) — \textquotedblleft{}because of, due to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جاده} \fa{به} \fa{دلیل} \fa{برف} \fa{بسته} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jâdde be dalil-e barf baste shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The road was closed because of snow.
\end{quote}

Takes a noun with ezafe; with a clause, \emph{be dalil-e inke} … .

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{دلیل}} joins the Persian preposition \emph{be} to \emph{dalil}, from Arabic \emph{dalīl} (EtymDB glosses it \textquotedblleft{}guide\textquotedblright{}): by reason of.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be dalil-e}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{be dalil-e}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to lead to, then the Persian for to conclude, then say \emph{be dalil-e} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{به} \fa{همین} \fa{دلیل} (be hamin dalil)}{به همین دلیل (be hamin dalil)}]{\fa{به} \fa{همین} \fa{دلیل} (be hamin dalil) — for this reason, that is why}

\label{lesson:FA-C371-be-hamin-dalil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to conclude, then the Persian for because of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{به} \fa{همین} \fa{دلیل}}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{همین} \fa{دلیل}} (\emph{be hamin dalil}) — \textquotedblleft{}for this reason, that is why\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کارش} \fa{را} \fa{دوست} \fa{نداشت،} \fa{به} \fa{همین} \fa{دلیل} \fa{دنبال} \fa{یک} \fa{کار} \fa{تازه} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kârash râ dust nadâsht, be hamin dalil donbâl-e yek kâr-e tâze ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He did not like his job; that is why he is looking for a new one.
\end{quote}

\emph{Be} + \emph{hamin} \textquotedblleft{}this very\textquotedblright{} + \emph{dalil} \textquotedblleft{}reason\textquotedblright{}. It opens a clause that states a result.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{همین} \fa{دلیل}} joins the native words \emph{be} \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{} and \emph{hamin} \textquotedblleft{}this very\textquotedblright{} to \emph{dalil}, from Arabic \emph{dalīl} (EtymDB): for this very reason.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be hamin dalil}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{be hamin dalil}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to conclude, then the Persian for because of, then say \emph{be hamin dalil} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{از} \fa{این} \fa{رو} (az in ru)}{از این رو (az in ru)}]{\fa{از} \fa{این} \fa{رو} (az in ru) — hence, for this reason}

\label{lesson:FA-C371-az-in-ru}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for because of, then the Persian for for this reason.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{از} \fa{این} \fa{رو}}
\textbf{\fa{از} \fa{این} \fa{رو}} (\emph{az in ru}) — \textquotedblleft{}hence, for this reason\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قیمتها} \fa{بالا} \fa{رفت،} \fa{از} \fa{این} \fa{رو} \fa{مردم} \fa{کمتر} \fa{خرید} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qeymathâ bâlâ raft, az in ru mardom kamtar kharid kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Prices went up; hence people bought less.
\end{quote}

Formal, mostly written. \emph{Az} \textquotedblleft{}from\textquotedblright{} + \emph{in} \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{} + \emph{ru} \textquotedblleft{}face, side\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{از} \fa{این} \fa{رو}} is native Persian, literally \textquotedblleft{}from this face\textquotedblright{}: \emph{az} \textquotedblleft{}from\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB traces it to Old Persian), \emph{in} \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ru} \textquotedblleft{}face, side\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{az in ru}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{az in ru}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{az in ru}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for because of, then the Persian for for this reason, then say \emph{az in ru} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{لذا} (lezâ)}{لذا (lezâ)}]{\fa{لذا} (lezâ) — therefore (formal)}

\label{lesson:FA-C371-leza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for for this reason, then the Persian for hence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{لذا}}
\textbf{\fa{لذا}} (\emph{lezâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}therefore (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هوا} \fa{خیلی} \fa{بد} \fa{بود،} \fa{لذا} \fa{جلسه} \fa{برگزار} \fa{نشد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{havâ kheyli bad bud, lezâ jalase bargozâr nashod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather was very bad; therefore the meeting was not held.
\end{quote}

Formal and written; in speech \emph{barâye hamin}. A whole clause follows. \fa{ذ} sounds like z.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{لذا}} is usually traced to the Arabic phrase \emph{li-dhā} \textquotedblleft{}for this\textquotedblright{}; Persian says the Arabic \emph{dh} as \emph{z}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lezâ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lezâ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{lezâ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for for this reason, then the Persian for hence, then say \emph{lezâ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{با} \fa{توجه} \fa{به} (bâ tavajjoh be)}{با توجه به (bâ tavajjoh be)}]{\fa{با} \fa{توجه} \fa{به} (bâ tavajjoh be) — considering, given}

\label{lesson:FA-C371-ba-tavajjoh-be}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for hence, then the Persian for therefore.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{با} \fa{توجه} \fa{به}}
\textbf{\fa{با} \fa{توجه} \fa{به}} (\emph{bâ tavajjoh be}) — \textquotedblleft{}considering, given\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{با} \fa{توجه} \fa{به} \fa{قیمت،} \fa{این} \fa{ماشین} \fa{خوب} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bâ tavajjoh be qeymat, in mâshin khub ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Considering the price, this car is good.
\end{quote}

\emph{Bâ} \textquotedblleft{}with\textquotedblright{} + \emph{tavajjoh} \textquotedblleft{}attention\textquotedblright{} + \emph{be} \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{}. It takes a noun; with a clause, \emph{bâ tavajjoh be inke} … .

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{با} \fa{توجه} \fa{به}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}with attention to\textquotedblright{}: \emph{bâ} and \emph{be} are Persian, and \emph{tavajjoh} \textquotedblleft{}attention\textquotedblright{} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{tawajjuh} \textquotedblleft{}turning towards\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bâ tavajjoh be}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for hence, then the Persian for therefore, then say \emph{bâ tavajjoh be} again
\end{itemize}
